::: {#sol-momentum-long-run}

Unrolling $\vv_t = \beta \vv_{t - 1} + \vg$ from $\vv_0 = \vzero$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vv_t
&= \vg + \beta \vg + \dots + \beta^{t - 1} \vg
&& \text{(apply the update $t$ times)} \\
&= \frac{1 - \beta^t}{1 - \beta} \vg
&& \text{(sum of a geometric series, for $0 \le \beta < 1$)} \\
&\to \frac{1}{1 - \beta} \vg
&& \text{(since $\beta^t \to 0$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So the step approaches $\frac{\learnrate}{1 - \beta} \vg$:
on a steady slope,
momentum moves like plain [gradient descent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/optimization.html#def-gradient-descent) with [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) $\learnrate / (1 - \beta)$.
With $\beta = 0.9$ that is 10 times $\learnrate$.

:::
